docs.title: CoastDiff
docs.text:
Diffusion-based coastal downscaling driven by ERA5. Give it a latitude/longitude box and a time (a single hour, or a continuous range such as every hour for three days), and it produces ~3 km fields of eight surface variables from ERA5 (~25 km) with a two-stage CorrDiff model: a deterministic regression network followed by a diffusion model that restores small-scale detail.

  • Input: ERA5 only, read live from the public ARCO ERA5 archive. Nothing to download beforehand.
  • Output: one NetCDF file per hour, with the deterministic prediction and a diffusion ensemble.
  • Inference only: no training or test data is included.
  • Lightweight install: the normalization statistics are bundled; the two trained checkpoints (~640 MB) are downloaded once from Zenodo on first use. torch is the only machine-learning dependency.

docs.title: Citation
docs.text:
Ranjbar, S. (2026). CoastDiff pretrained checkpoints: two-stage CorrDiff coastal downscaling of ERA5 (regression + diffusion) (v1.0.0). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23510727

Note

A manuscript describing CoastDiff is in prep.

docs.title: Authors
docs.text: Sadegh Ranjbar, Lucas Gloege, Elizabeth Yankovsky Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences, Yale University, New Haven, CT, United States of America

docs.title: License
docs.text:
Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0

The model code in src/coastdiff/models/vendor/ is adapted from NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo and its CorrDiff implementation. NVIDIA Corporation is the developer of the underlying two-stage regression + diffusion architecture, the EDM preconditioning and the sampler that this package deploys, also licensed under Apache 2.0. The code has been trimmed to the architecture the bundled checkpoints use and no longer needs PhysicsNeMo installed. See NOTICE for the attribution and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for how the adaptation was verified against the original.

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
Two-stage CorrDiff (NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo architecture; see "No PhysicsNeMo dependency" below):

  1. Regression UNet — deterministic mean prediction, 32x32 (34ch) coarse input -> 256x256 (8ch) high-resolution output.
  2. EDM diffusion residual model — conditioned on the regression mean, samples a stochastic residual restoring small-scale detail the regression network smooths away. Run per ensemble member.

Both stages are loaded from checkpoint directories configured in src/coastdiff/configs/default.yaml; the highest training-iteration checkpoint in each directory is used (see models/checkpoint_loader.find_latest_checkpoint).

docs.title: No PhysicsNeMo dependency
docs.text:
CoastDiff does not need NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo installed: importing it at runtime would be a heavyweight, somewhat fragile prerequisite (pinned warp-lang, a specific clone). The model code actually needed is a small slice of PhysicsNeMo:

  • the UNet backbone (SongUNetPosEmbd and its layer building blocks: conv/group-norm/attention/embedding layers),
  • the two wrapper classes the checkpoints were saved as (CorrDiffRegressionUNet, EDMPrecondSuperResolution),
  • the EDM stochastic sampler, and
  • the regression_step/diffusion_step orchestration functions.

This slice (~4,500 lines) is vendored directly into src/coastdiff/models/vendor/ (adapted from PhysicsNeMo, Apache-2.0 — see NOTICE), with PhysicsNeMo's own model-registry/checkpoint-format machinery (the physicsnemo.core.Module base class, .mdlus file I/O) replaced by a small local shim (vendor/_compat.py) and loader (vendor/checkpoint_io.py). torch is the only ML-framework dependency left.

Verification. Architecture-preserving edits like this are easy to get subtly wrong (a missing layer, a renamed parameter), so this wasn't just reviewed by eye:

  1. Every vendored model class (CorrDiffRegressionUNet, EDMPrecondSuperResolution) is instantiated from the real checkpoints' own saved init arguments, and its state_dict() keys and tensor shapes are compared against the checkpoint's raw, unmodified state_dict -- confirmed to match exactly (676/676 parameters, both checkpoints, zero missing/extra/mismatched-shape keys).
  2. A full end-to-end run (ERA5 fetch → regression → stochastic diffusion sampling → stitched output) was executed on the same region, timestamp, and seed through both the PhysicsNeMo-backed implementation and the vendored one. Every output channel — input_era5, unet, and corrdiff (all ensemble members, i.e. including the random diffusion sampling path, not just the deterministic regression) — matched bit-for-bit.

docs.title: Input: ERA5
docs.text: This package is inference-only and ERA5-only. The model was trained on HRRR fields coarsened to a ~24 km grid (README, "How the model was trained"); at inference the same 34 coarse channels are built from ERA5. ERA5 is fetched directly from the public ARCO Zarr store and regridded (bilinear) onto each patch's own coarse grid — see data/era5.py. Derived channels (q_sfc, tp_in, radiation unit conversion, cos_sza) are computed after regridding the raw fields, because the dew-point-to-humidity relation is nonlinear. ERA5 and the coarsened HRRR training inputs differ physically (clouds, radiation, aerosols, precipitation), so ERA5-driven output is not identical in character to what the model saw in training.

docs.title: Geographic coverage: one grid, any region
docs.text:
No region-specific data is bundled and there is no domain check. Every request is handled by the same code path:

  • Output grid: grid.build_generic_grid builds a regular lat/lon grid at ~3km spacing on the fly for the requested box (latitude spacing is fixed, since 1° latitude is ~111km everywhere; longitude spacing is adjusted for the region's central latitude so cells stay close to 3km x 3km in real distance).
  • Invariant channels (elevation, land-sea mask): sourced from ERA5's own global static fields, geopotential_at_surface (÷ 9.80665 -> elevation in m) and land_sea_mask, regridded (bilinear) onto that same grid (Era5RawRegion.global_invariants, data/era5.py).

This works anywhere on Earth because the convolutional architecture has no geographic restriction baked in: its positional embeddings (SongUNetPosEmbd, gridtype="sinusoidal") are computed purely from linspace(0, 2π, patch_size), i.e. position within a 256x256 patch, with no dependency on absolute lat/lon.

The model was trained for regional coastal areas (ocean-dominated patches in the HRRR domain). It can be run anywhere ERA5 has data, but skill outside the trained coastal regimes has not been evaluated. The training grid was a Lambert conformal projection with HRRR-native ~3km terrain and land-sea fields; the output grid here is a regular lat/lon grid and the terrain and land-sea fields are ERA5's ~25km ones. Each output file's grid_source attribute records this (generic_global).

docs.title: Tiling and stitching
docs.text: A requested region is tiled into overlapping 256x256-pixel patches on the native grid (--overlap, default 3px). Each patch is inferred independently and stitched back with trapezoidal-weight feathering across the overlap band, so seams blend smoothly. NaN appears wherever the requested region falls outside the requested box, or ERA5 data was unavailable for that pixel.

docs.title: Continuous time ranges and parallelism
docs.text: ERA5 is fetched once per run for the whole requested time span (not once per timestamp). Each run is single-device, as CorrDiff is; there is no in-process multi-GPU. Timestamps and sub-regions are independent, so throughput is scaled by launching several runs at once, one GPU each, split by time or space — see the README section "GPU usage and parallelizing".

docs.title: Rain filter
docs.text: tp (precipitation) is the most spatially intermittent output variable, and diffusion's stochastic texture is most valuable exactly where real rain is occurring — and mostly just noise elsewhere. rain_filter.py blends the deterministic unet prediction with the diffusion corrdiff prediction, keyed on unet's own predicted rain rate exceeding a threshold (default 0.02mm; --rain-filter-mm changes it, --no-rain-filter disables it).

docs.title: Physical constraints
docs.text: physical_constraints.py runs after the rain filter and the tp conversion to mm, on the unet and corrdiff fields only (input_era5 is written as fetched): tp, ssrd and strd are clipped to be non-negative, and ssrd is set to zero wherever cos(solar zenith angle) <= 0. The cosine is computed per output pixel from latitude, longitude and the timestamp with the same simple declination/hour-angle formula as the model's cos_sza input channel (no equation of time or refraction, so pixels within a few minutes of sunset can be zeroed slightly early). Longwave is not zeroed at night; NaN is kept.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Requires Python 3.11+, internet access (to read ERA5 and, once, to download the checkpoints), and preferably one NVIDIA GPU (the CPU works but is slow). Create an environment, then install straight from GitHub:

Note

CoastDiff will soon be available on PyPi

UV 

uv init --bare --no-pin-python
uv add git+https://github.com/CDR-Forecasting-Stack/coastdiff.git
coastdiff --help

Conda 

conda create -n coastdiff python=3.11 -y && conda activate coastdiff
pip install git+https://github.com/CDR-Forecasting-Stack/coastdiff.git
coastdiff --help

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
For development, clone the repository and run pip install -e . instead.

Checkpoints. The first run downloads the two checkpoints (~640 MB) from Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23510727) into ~/.cache/coastdiff/checkpoints/, verifies their SHA-256, and reuses them afterwards. To fetch them by hand, download both .mdlus files from the Zenodo record into ~/.cache/coastdiff/checkpoints/regression/ and .../diffusion/ respectively.

pyproject.toml pins torch and zarr to versions verified against the bundled checkpoints and the ERA5 archive. Keep them pinned: unpinned upgrades have broken checkpoint loading and Zarr access. No NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo installation is needed (see License).

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
The package ships with a worked example: the Gulf of Mexico during the three days of a tropical cyclone's Florida landfall, hourly.

bash examples/run_example.sh --quick      # one hour, about a minute
bash examples/run_example.sh              # all 72 hours, about 20-25 minutes on one GPU (~16 s per hour)
python examples/run_example.py [--quick]  # the same through the Python API, with a summary

Your own region and time:

# a single hour
coastdiff --lat-min 24 --lat-max 31 --lon-min -98 --lon-max -80 --timestamp "2026-10-09 12:00"

# every 3 hours for two days, 8 diffusion members, results in ./results
coastdiff --lat-min 30 --lat-max 45 --lon-min -130 --lon-max -115 \
          --start "2025-07-15 00:00" --end "2025-07-16 21:00" --interval 3h \
          --num-ensembles 8 --output-dir results

Python:

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from coastdiff import run_inference

paths = run_inference(
    lat_min=24, lat_max=31, lon_min=-98, lon_max=-80,
    timestamps=[datetime(2026, 10, 9, 12, tzinfo=timezone.utc)],
    output_dir="outputs",
)

Longitudes are degrees east (west is negative); all times are UTC.

docs.title: Defaults
docs.text:
Running coastdiff with no arguments uses these (all can be changed):

setting default region Gulf of Mexico: 24-31 N, 98-80 W time 2026-10-08 00:00 to 2026-10-10 23:00 UTC, every hour (72 files) output folder outputs/ (relative to where you run it) diffusion ensemble members 4 patch overlap 3 pixels rain filter on, 0.02 mm device the GPU if one is visible, otherwise the CPU

docs.title: Model inputs and outputs
docs.text:
Input (34 channels + 2 fixed fields). For every patch the model receives ERA5 on a 32 x 32 grid (~24 km), upsampled to the 256 x 256 grid (~3 km) the model works on, plus two fixed fields on that fine grid. Everything comes from ERA5; the channel order is fixed by the trained weights.

group channels unit ERA5 variable surface wind u10, v10 m/s 10m u/v component of wind surface temperature t2m, d2m K 2m temperature, 2m dewpoint temperature pressure sp, msl Pa surface pressure, mean sea level pressure humidity q_sfc kg/kg derived from d2m and sp column water tcwv kg/m2 total column water vapour radiation ssrd, strd W/m2 surface solar / thermal radiation downwards (hourly mean) precipitation tp_in mm total precipitation (1 h) cloud, land tcc, lsm 0-1 total cloud cover, land-sea mask upper air, 1000/850/500/250 hPa u, v (m/s), z (m), t (K), q (kg/kg) wind, geopotential height, temperature, specific humidity solar geometry cos_sza 0-1 cosine of the solar zenith angle (computed) fixed fields (2) elev_mean (m), lsm_mean (0-1) ERA5 surface geopotential / 9.80665, and land-sea mask

The channels are named exactly this way in the input_era5 output group.

Output (8 channels, ~3 km).

variable meaning unit 2t 2 m air temperature K 10u, 10v 10 m wind components m/s tp precipitation (1 h accumulation) mm ssrd downward shortwave radiation at the surface W/m2 strd downward longwave radiation at the surface W/m2 sp surface pressure Pa q near-surface specific humidity kg/kg

Every output field is in the same plain physical unit as its input counterpart.

docs.title: How the model was trained
docs.text:
CoastDiff is a two-stage CorrDiff model (NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo architecture): a regression network predicts the mean ~3 km field from a 32 x 32 coarse input, and an EDM diffusion model samples the residual that restores small-scale structure. It was trained on NOAA HRRR analyses (surface and pressure-level GRIB2 files), with the 34 coarse input channels above and 8 high-resolution target channels.

  • Training data: 120,000 training samples, taken from 1,200 random hourly times over 2018-2023, 100 coastal patches of 256 x 256 HRRR pixels (~3 km) per time. Each patch has an ocean centre pixel and is at least 70 % ocean.
  • Coarse input: the native HRRR fields were low-pass filtered with a 50 km GCM-Filters scale and then conservatively regridded (xESMF) to the 32 x 32 grid (~24 km).
  • Training length: regression network 5,000,000 samples; diffusion model 50,000,000 samples.
  • Testing: on independent data by temporal cross-validation: training on 2018-2023, testing on 10,000 patches from 2024-2025.

ERA5 is used only at inference, as the model's input.

docs.title: Geographic coverage and limitations
docs.text:
The model was trained for regional coastal areas: ocean-dominated patches inside the HRRR domain (roughly 21-53 N, 134-61 W: the contiguous US and its coastal waters). CoastDiff places no restriction on where you run it: it works for any region and any time ERA5 covers, and the Gulf of Mexico example is just one choice. Results outside the coastal regimes it was trained on have not been evaluated.

  • Output grid: a regular latitude/longitude grid of ~3 km spacing is built for each request (latitude spacing is fixed; longitude spacing is scaled by the cosine of the central latitude). The training grid was a Lambert conformal projection, so cells are close to, but not exactly, 3 km x 3 km.
  • Fixed fields: elevation and land-sea mask come from ERA5 (~25 km). The model was trained with these at ~3 km, so fine terrain and coastline detail is coarser than in training.
  • Extreme precipitation: in intense systems such as tropical-cyclone cores the model can produce hourly rain far above what the ~25 km ERA5 input suggests (in the Gulf example, peak values near 180 mm per hour against about 15 mm per hour in the ERA5 input). Treat precipitation extremes as unvalidated.
  • Input differences: ERA5 and the coarsened HRRR fields used in training differ physically (clouds, radiation, aerosols and precipitation in particular), so ERA5-driven output is not identical in character to what the model saw during training.

docs.title: Time ranges and ERA5 availability
docs.text:
--start, --end and --interval (for example 1h, 6h, 1d) request many times at once. ERA5 is read once for the whole span (one request per variable, not per hour), and each hour is regridded and run from that in-memory block, so a long range costs far less input/output than separate single-hour runs. --end is inclusive.

ERA5 is published a few days after real time, and the public archive can be missing individual hours or days (recent days are sometimes written late). Before doing any work, CoastDiff probes every requested hour and, if some are missing, stops and lists exactly which ones. Add --skip-missing (skip_missing=True in Python) to run only the hours that exist; the skipped hours are logged and no file is written for them. The examples use --skip-missing, so they run even if the archive has a gap.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
One NetCDF4 file per hour: <output-dir>/coastdiff_<YYYYMMDD>T<HHMM>.nc with three groups.

group contents dimensions input_era5 the model's 34 coarse input channels time, y_lr, x_lr (~24 km) unet regression-only (deterministic) prediction, 8 variables time, y, x (~3 km) corrdiff regression + diffusion prediction, 8 variables, one slice per ensemble member time, ensemble, y, x

Every group carries CF-convention coordinates: a real time coordinate and 2-D lat/lon arrays, so each group opens on its own:

import xarray as xr
ds = xr.open_dataset("outputs/coastdiff_20261009T1200.nc", group="corrdiff")
ds["2t"]                       # (time, ensemble, y, x), kelvin
ds.lat, ds.lon                 # 2-D coordinates

# join many hours into one time series
all_hours = xr.open_mfdataset("outputs/coastdiff_*.nc", group="unet", combine="by_coords")

NaN marks pixels outside the requested box or without ERA5 data. Global attributes record the region, time, checkpoints used, rain-filter threshold and a description of the fields.

docs.title: Rain filter and physical constraints
docs.text:
Rain filter (on by default). For corrdiff, tp uses the deterministic unet value except where unet predicts more than 0.02 mm of rain, where the diffusion value is used. This avoids diffusion noise in dry areas while keeping the textured detail where it is raining. Change the threshold with --rain-filter-mm, or switch it off with --no-rain-filter.

Physical constraints (always applied to unet and corrdiff; input_era5 is left as fetched). - tp, ssrd and strd are never negative. - ssrd (shortwave) is zero wherever the sun is at or below the horizon (solar zenith angle of 90 degrees or more), computed for each output pixel from its position and the time. Longwave is not zeroed at night. - Missing pixels stay NaN.

docs.title: GPU usage and parallelizing
docs.text:
CoastDiff is designed to use one GPU per run, like CorrDiff itself: it uses the GPU it can see (or the CPU if there is none) and has no GPU-count option. To pick a GPU, restrict what the process can see, for example CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 coastdiff ....

To go faster, run several independent jobs at once (one GPU each), splitting the work by time or by space:

  • By time: each job takes a different slice of the time range. Hours are independent, so the results are identical to one long run.
  • By space: each job takes a different sub-region (a smaller --lat-min/--lat-max/--lon-min/--lon-max). Give every sub-region its own --output-dir: file names contain only the time, so jobs sharing a folder would overwrite each other. Each sub-region builds its own grid and its patches do not blend across the sub-region edge, so overlap the boxes slightly if you plan to merge them.

SLURM templates are in scripts/: run_inference.sbatch (one job) and run_inference_array.sbatch (a job array that splits a time range across GPUs). Add your cluster's partition/account lines and environment activation to them. By hand, four independent jobs:

for start in "2026-10-08 00:00" "2026-10-08 18:00" "2026-10-09 12:00" "2026-10-10 06:00"; do
  end=$(date -u -d "$start + 17 hours" "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
  sbatch scripts/run_inference.sbatch --start "$start" --end "$end" --interval 1h
done

docs.title: Command-line options
docs.text:
option default meaning --lat-min, --lat-max, --lon-min, --lon-max 24, 31, -98, -80 region (degrees; west longitudes negative) --timestamp none a single UTC time, e.g. "2026-10-09 12:00" --start, --end, --interval 2026-10-08 00:00, 2026-10-10 23:00, 1h a time range (--end inclusive; interval like 1h, 6h, 1d) --output-dir outputs where the NetCDF files are written --num-ensembles 4 diffusion ensemble members --overlap 3 pixel overlap between neighbouring patches (0 = none) --rain-filter-mm / --no-rain-filter 0.02 / off rain-filter threshold, or disable it --skip-missing off run only the hours ERA5 has, instead of stopping when some are missing --mode all regression skips the diffusion model for a fast deterministic preview --sampler, --sampler-steps, --solver stochastic, model default, euler diffusion sampler settings --seed, --seed-batch-size 0, 1 random seed; ensemble members run per batch --config src/coastdiff/configs/default.yaml alternative configuration file

coastdiff --help prints the same list.

docs.title: Updating the model
docs.text: The checkpoints are published on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23510727) and cached in ~/.cache/coastdiff/checkpoints/{regression,diffusion}/; the normalization statistics (src/coastdiff/assets/stats.json) are bundled with the package. src/coastdiff/configs/default.yaml points at the checkpoint folders, and the highest-iteration .mdlus file in each is chosen on every run. To use a newly trained model, add its two .mdlus files to those folders (or point the config at other folders with --config) and replace stats.json with the statistics of the same training run (the statistics are not chosen automatically, and they must match the weights). Only the inference weights (.mdlus) are needed, not optimizer state.

docs.title: Repository layout and tests
docs.text:
coastdiff/
  README.md  LICENSE  NOTICE  pyproject.toml
  examples/                   run_example.py, run_example.sh
  scripts/                    SLURM templates
  docs/ARCHITECTURE.md        how it works and how the model code was verified
  tests/
  src/coastdiff/
    configs/default.yaml      checkpoint folders, statistics path, output folder, rain-filter default
    assets/stats.json         per-channel mean / standard deviation (34 input, 8 output)
    cli.py                    command-line entry point
    inference.py              the pipeline: grid, ERA5, tiling, model, stitching, output
    output.py                 NetCDF writer
    rain_filter.py            physical_constraints.py   time_utils.py   config.py
    data/                     ERA5 fetch and regrid, channel/unit tables, grid and tiling, normalization
    models/                   checkpoint loading and Zenodo download; vendor/ holds the model code

Run the tests (the model tests need the checkpoints, downloaded on first use if absent; the rest need no network):

pip install -e ".[test]"
python -m pytest tests -q
